/-!
# Erdős Problem 785

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/785](https://www.erdosproblems.com/785)
- [ChFa10] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2010), 1923-1927.
- [ChFa11] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On additive complements. II*. Proc. Amer. Math. Soc.
  (2011), 881-883.
- [ChFa14] Fang, Jin-Hui and Chen, Yong-Gao, *On additive complements. III*. J. Number Theory
  (2014), 83-91.
- [ChFa15] Chen, Yong-Gao and Fang, Jin-Hui, *On a conjecture of Sárközy and Szemerédi*.
  Acta Arith. (2015), 47-58.
- [Da64] Danzer, L., *Über eine Frage von G. Hanani aus der additiven Zahlentheorie*.
  J. Reine Angew. Math. (1964), 392-394.
- [Er57] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Michigan Math. J. (1957), 291-300.
- [Er61] Erdős, Paul, *Some unsolved problems*. Magyar Tud. Akad. Mat. Kutató Int. Közl. (1961),
  221-254.
- [Na59] Narkiewicz, Władysław, *Remarks on a conjecture of Hanani in additive number theory*.
  Colloq. Math. (1959/60), 161-165.
- [Ru17] Ruzsa, Imre Z., *Exact additive complements*. Q. J. Math. (2017), 227-235.
- [SaSz94] Sárközy, A. and Szemerédi, E., *On a problem in additive number theory*.
  Acta Math. Hungar. (1994), 237-245.

open Filter Pointwise
open scoped Topology

namespace Erdos785

/-- The counting function $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$. -/
noncomputable def counting (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x).ncard

/-- The largest element of $A$ in $[1,x]$, that is $a^*(x)=\max A\cap [1,x]$
(equal to $0$ when there is no such element). -/
noncomputable def aStar (A : Set ℕ) (x : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  sSup (A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x)

/-- Two sets $A, B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ are *exact additive complements* if $A+B$ contains all
large integers and $A(x)B(x)\sim x$. -/
def IsExactAdditiveComplement (A B : Set ℕ) : Prop :=
  IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1)

/--
Let $A,B\subseteq \mathbb{N}$ be infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers.
Let $A(x)=\lvert A\cap [1,x]\rvert$ and similarly for $B(x)$. Is it true that if
$A(x)B(x)\sim x$ then
$$A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$$
as $x\to \infty$?

A conjecture of Erdős and Danzer. The answer is yes, proved by Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94],
who actually proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$

This was formalized in Lean by van Doorn using Aristotle.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem785.lean"]
theorem erdos_785 : answer(True) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → IsExactAdditiveComplement A B →
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Danzer [Da64] proved that exact additive complements exist (Hanani had earlier conjectured they
do not exist, as reported in [Er57] and [Er61]).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.danzer :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B := by
  sorry

/--
Sárközy and Szemerédi [SaSz94] proved that it is impossible for
$$A(x)B(x)-x=o(A(x)).$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.sarkozy_szemeredi (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =o[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa15] proved $A(x)B(x)-x\ll A(x)^c$ cannot hold for any constant $c>0$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) (c : ℝ) (hc : 0 < c) :
    ¬ (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) =O[atTop]
      (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x : ℝ) ^ c) := by
  sorry

/--
Narkiewicz [Na59] proved that, under the given assumptions (and perhaps swapping $A$ and $B$)
we must have $A(2x)/A(x)\to 1$ and $B(2x)/B(x)\to 2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∨
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$ and $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions
in the problem then (after possibly changing the roles of $A$ and $B$)
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) ∨
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar B x : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
      < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Chen conjectures that this should be true with $3/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → IsAdditiveComplement A B →
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          < ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos785

findings.description: The file mixes incompatible conventions: A and B are unrestricted `Set ℕ`, so `IsAdditiveComplement A B` permits representations using 0, but `counting` counts only `A ∩ Set.Icc 1 x`. Discarding 0 from a count is not harmless for the excess: if 0 belongs to A, it subtracts the unbounded quantity B(x) from the product. This makes `Erdos785.erdos_785`, `Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound`, `Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup`, and the proposition asked by `Erdos785.erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture` false. For a counterexample construction, take Ruzsa's positive exact complements with E(n)=A(n)B(n)-n<log n along an unbounded sequence, labelling B as the large side, so B(n)>n^(3/4) eventually. Put m=min A, C={a-m : a∈A}, and D={b+m : b∈B}. Their sumset is unchanged, and bounded changes to their counting functions preserve exactness. However, the file's excess at n-m is at most E(n)-B(n)+m, tending to minus infinity along that sequence. Their limsup ratio is still 1, so both limsup hypotheses hold; the Ruzsa lower bound fails already at ε=1. This is one shared domain/counting defect, rather than four independent errors.
findings.source_evidence: Ruzsa, *Exact additive complements*, Introduction and Theorems 1.1–1.3, https://arxiv.org/e-print/1510.00812, explicitly works with sets of positive integers. His Theorem 1.3 supplies the small-excess examples and Theorem 1.1 gives the small/large dichotomy. Chen–Fang [ChFa15], p. 47, https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82737, instead permits nonnegative integers but explicitly defines T(x)=|T∩[0,x]|. Neither source uses the file's mixed convention. The linked external `corollary_erdos_785` also explicitly assumes `h_pos_A` and `h_pos_B`, excluding zero.
findings.suggested_fix: Use one consistent convention throughout. Either retain `counting` on `[1,x]` and impose `0 ∉ A` and `0 ∉ B` in the relevant definitions/statements and existential witnesses, or retain unrestricted `Set ℕ` and change `counting A x` to `(A ∩ Set.Iic x).ncard`, updating the counting-function docstrings to `[0,x]`. The latter matches the Chen–Fang papers' nonnegative convention.

findings.description: The bound is denied for every labelled A and every c>0, but the cited result concerns the smaller complement. The statement is false even when both sets contain only positive integers, independently of the zero-counting defect. Choose the large side of an exact pair as A; Narkiewicz's dichotomy ensures B(n)≤A(n) eventually. Exactness gives n≤2A(n)B(n) eventually, hence |A(n)B(n)-n|≤3A(n)^2. Thus the Big-O assertion that this theorem negates holds for c=2. This implication was proved in the scratch file without using any sorry-backed problem theorem.
findings.source_evidence: Chen–Fang [ChFa15], Theorem 0.2, pp. 47–48, https://www.impan.pl/shop/en/publication/transaction/download/product/82737, proves E(x)≥min{A(x),B(x)}^M eventually for every M>1. Ruzsa's presentation at https://arxiv.org/e-print/1510.00812 says immediately before discussing the Sárközy–Szemerédi and Chen–Fang bounds: 'For the sequel we will assume ... A is small and B is large.' The A(x)^c formulation relies on that standing convention.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the comparison function by `(fun x : ℕ => (min (counting A x) (counting B x) : ℝ) ^ c)`. Alternatively, add the small-side hypothesis `Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2*x) : ℝ) / counting A x) atTop (𝓝 1)`. Also apply the file-wide counting/domain correction.

reformulations.difference: Unlike Ruzsa's presentation, the Lean little-o statement does not normalize A to be the smaller complement. This omission is harmless for little-o, although it is not harmless for the Chen–Fang Big-O variant.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For any two infinite sets, at every sufficiently large n∈B the excess satisfies E(n)-E(n-1)≥A(n)-1. If E=o(A), both E(n) and E(n-1) are o(A(n)), contradicting this jump as A(n)→∞. Thus the arbitrarily labelled assertion already holds without exactness. The scratch lemma `littleO_min_reformulation` proves its equivalence with the version using min(A(n),B(n)); the reverse direction uses the independent jump proof.

reformulations.difference: The source's `(1-o(1))` lower bound is expanded into `∀ ε>0, ∀ᶠ x, ...`, with a disjunction selecting the orientation once rather than separately for each x or ε.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For eventually positive g, the epsilon condition `(1-ε)g(n)<f(n)` eventually for every ε>0 is equivalent to existence of r(n)→0 with `(1-r(n))g(n)<f(n)` eventually. In the forward direction take r(n)=max(0,1-f(n)/g(n))+1/(n+1); conversely use r(n)<ε eventually. This equivalence was proved as `epsilon_lower_iff_vanishing_error`. Here g=aStar/counting is eventually positive for an infinite set. The disjunction correctly implements a fixed swap of A and B. This validates the asymptotic expansion, not the separate file-wide domain error.

review.notes: All three definitions and ten theorems were checked. The shared zero/counting defect is reported once at file level. `/workspace/review/scratch.lean` compiles with no errors or warnings; the counting-growth lemma, little-o proof, large-side Big-O bound and two equivalence proofs use no `sorryAx`. Finite tests confirm that ncard and aStar have the stated empty-input values, and the EReal limsup avoids the unbounded-real default-value issue. The Chen–Fang sharpness example still has valid positive witnesses: shifting both binary digit sets by 1 preserves excess 1 at n=4^k-1 and the limsup 3/2. Full original texts of [Da64], [SaSz94] and [ChFa14] were unavailable, but their relevant statements were verified in other cited papers and Chen's slides. The cited page records the intended main problem as proved in Lean and still presents the 3/2 assertion as a conjecture; no separate stale-status issue was established. No repository files were changed.

-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.narkiewicz (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 2)) ∨
    (Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting B (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 1) ∧
      Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A (2 * x) : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ))
        atTop (𝓝 2)) := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] has constructed, for any function $w(x)\to \infty$, such a pair of sets with
$$A(x)B(x)-x<w(x)$$
for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_upper_bound (w : ℕ → ℝ) (hw : Tendsto w atTop atTop) :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsExactAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) < w x := by
  sorry

/--
Ruzsa [Ru17] proves that, if $a^*(x)=\max A \cap [1,x]$ and $A$ and $B$ satisfy the conditions
in the problem then (after possibly changing the roles of $A$ and $B$)
$$A(x)B(x)-x > (1-o(1))\frac{a^*(x)}{A(x)}.$$
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.ruzsa_lower_bound (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsExactAdditiveComplement A B) :
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar A x : ℝ) / (counting A x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) ∨
    (∀ ε > (0 : ℝ), ∀ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop,
        (1 - ε) * (aStar B x : ℝ) / (counting B x : ℝ)
          < (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Chen and Fang [ChFa10] proved the stronger statement that $A(x)B(x)-x\to \infty$ if $A$ and $B$
are infinite sets such that $A+B$ contains all large integers and
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}<\frac{5}{4}.$$
They later [ChFa14] improved $5/4$ to $3-\sqrt{3}\approx 1.268$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_limsup (A B : Set ℕ) (hA : A.Infinite) (hB : B.Infinite)
    (h : IsAdditiveComplement A B)
    (hlim : limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
      < ((3 - Real.sqrt 3 : ℝ) : EReal)) :
    Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
Chen conjectures that this should be true with $3/2$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_conjecture : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite → B.Infinite → IsAdditiveComplement A B →
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          < ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) →
        Tendsto (fun x : ℕ => (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ)) atTop atTop := by
  sorry

/--
This is sharp, as Chen and Fang [ChFa11] also proved that there exist such $A$ and $B$ with
$$\limsup_{x\to \infty}\frac{A(x)B(x)}{x}=\frac{3}{2}$$
for which $A(x)B(x)-x=1$ for infinitely many $x$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_785.variants.chen_fang_sharp :
    ∃ A B : Set ℕ, A.Infinite ∧ B.Infinite ∧ IsAdditiveComplement A B ∧
      limsup (fun x : ℕ => ((counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) / (x : ℝ) : EReal)) atTop
          = ((3 / 2 : ℝ) : EReal) ∧
      ∃ᶠ x : ℕ in atTop, (counting A x * counting B x : ℝ) - (x : ℝ) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Erdos785
